title: Is there a true catch-22?
question: Does any pair of permits each require the other first, so that neither can be obtained?
finding: No. Among the 60 "before" pairs no permit is stated to need, directly or through a chain, a permit that needs it first. 6 pairs of pages that point at each other were read side by side; in every one the pages state which comes first. The published pages describe many permits stacked in sequence, not a circle.
how: The "before" pairs were searched for any path that returns to its starting permit. Separately, every case where two pages each name the other's permit was read and both sentences are shown with the order they state.
limits: This covers the wording of public pages. A loop could still arise in practice from a form, a code section or an office habit that the pages do not describe, and the consolidated codes were not available. The Street Space permit page and the Public Works completeness checklist of August 2026 do not ask for an issued building permit, although the Public Works forms have a box for a building permit number.

columns.t: What the pages say about order

rows.pair: Street vending permit and the health permit for a food vendor
rows.firstSentence: If you are selling prepackaged food and drink you must have a health permit from DPH.
rows.secondSentence: Required health and/or fire permits must be obtained within 90 days after approval of a Public Works permit.
rows.orderStated: Each page names the other permit, but the order is stated: the Public Works vending permit comes first and the health or fire permit must follow within 90 days.

secondPage.t: Learn about "Type 90” liquor licenses for music venues

rows.orderStated: The license needs the Board finding and the Board finding needs a license application, but only the application has to be filed first; the license is issued afterwards.

rows.pair: Building permit and Public Works street permits
rows.firstSentence: the basement needs structural work or upgrades, apply for a DBI building permit first, before applying for the Street Improvement and Minor Sidewalk Encroachment Permits.
rows.secondSentence: All required permits must be approved and issued before DBI can issue a Temporary Certificate of Occupancy (TCO) or Certificate of Final Completion and Occupancy
rows.orderStated: The building permit is applied for first, the street permits follow, and all of them must be issued before the certificate of occupancy, not before the building permit.

rows.firstSentence: must first receive a Planning Department Approval Letter (also known as a Zoning Approval Letter) before submitting an application to the Department of Building Inspection.
rows.secondSentence: submits a Building Permit to the Department of Building Inspection (DBI), the Planning Department is the first reviewing agency and will conduct the Neighborhood Notification.
rows.orderStated: One page says to get the Planning approval letter before filing with Building Inspection; another describes filing the building permit and Planning reviewing it first. Two routes are described; neither requires the other to be finished first.
